steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: (*whispers*) Sorry.

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: Ma'am! Hold on, please!

steps.name: Friendly Resident
steps.text: Oh, Reed! It's you! You left so suddenly—I was worried our hospitality had been lacking in some way.

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: No, I truly appreciated your hospitality. I had just suddenly remembered some business I had to take care of. I still have a few questions, though. Would you mind answering them for me?

steps.name: Friendly Resident
steps.text: Ask away.

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: Do you realize that you're engulfed in flames?

steps.name: Friendly Resident
steps.text: Flames? Oh, you mean my blessing? Wow, you can see other people's blessings?

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: I didn't notice until someone pointed it out to me—

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: Wait, you're saying you know about the flames, but can't see them? How can that be?
The friendly resident puts her hand on her waist.
The ancient Tarans carried small flames at their waists, stabilized through Originium Arts, to dispel the dark mist in the marsh.
After Victoria seized full control of Tara, this custom—along with all similar practices—was strictly banned.
But times have changed. No longer bound by Victoria's rules, the Tarans, or at least the people of Na Saoirsí, have chosen to wear small Originium lamps at their waists.

steps.name: Friendly Resident
steps.text: I'm sure you know fuel is scarce, and with the curfew in place, we can't afford to keep the lamps on—nor do we need to. But... if we carry these small lamps...

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: That's her fire... That's the color of her fire in the lamp.

steps.name: Friendly Resident
steps.text: Now, whenever people turn on their lamps, this is the color they'll see. Even if they replace the filaments with different ones, the color remains unchanged.

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: And you're not the least bit worried about this?

steps.name: Friendly Resident
steps.text: Well, as you can see, things are on the up and up here in Na Saoirsí. And what explanation can there be but the Red Dragon's blessing?

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: But—
But?
But if a reckless returnee tried to warn her that those flames were anything but fortuitous, she would never believe it.
Loughshinny hopes that perhaps a more direct approach would work.

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: But I wanted to experience the dragon's blessing for myself. May I hold your hand?

steps.name: Friendly Resident
steps.text: But you've already entered the city. Everyone who does will receive the blessing, sooner or later.

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: Please? It's just a small favor.

steps.name: Friendly Resident
steps.text: Well, I suppose it wasn't easy for you to make it all the way back to Tara.

steps.name: Friendly Resident
steps.text: Oh, right, what do you do for a living, anyway?

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: I... I know some basic medicine, along with some healing Arts. Nothing to brag about.

steps.name: Friendly Resident
steps.text: So you're a doctor, then. We're in need of doctors, actually.

steps.name: Friendly Resident
steps.text: Come here. Give me your hand—
She tightly clasps the woman's calloused hand, letting the fire spread from her own wrist to Loughshinny's.

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: Thank you...
She shuts her eyes.
Close your eyes and remember those whose pain you once soothed, those no longer forced to linger in this realm—
Go, and warm this cold fire.

steps.name: Friendly Resident
steps.text: Ugh...
The purple flames gradually fade. Beneath them, a pale face emerges, swaying gently, with a friendly smile.
So she tries to erase more of the purple flames, but fails to notice when the woman's expression suddenly changes.

steps.name: Friendly Resident
steps.text: My God, I—

steps.name: Friendly Resident
steps.text: My hand! What did you do to my hand?! It's completely numb!

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: What?!

steps.name: Friendly Resident
steps.text: I can't feel my blessing anymore, either! Just what are you doing to me?!

steps.name: Friendly Resident
steps.text: Let go!

steps.name: The Wakewoman
steps.text: Reed!

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: Wakewoman?

steps.name: The Wakewoman
steps.text: Reed, please let go of this poor lady.

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: I—

steps.name: The Wakewoman
steps.text: (Shakes head)

steps.name: The Wakewoman
steps.text: Sorry, ma'am.

steps.name: The Wakewoman
steps.text: She means no harm—I stake my honor on it.

steps.name: Friendly Resident
steps.text: But she said she's a doctor—how could a doctor possibly...?

steps.name: The Wakewoman
steps.text: Arts-based medicine can sometimes have side effects. Look at your hand, it's perfectly fine now, isn't it?

steps.name: Friendly Resident
steps.text: But I still can't feel anything—

steps.name: The Wakewoman
steps.text: You'll be fine.
The wayward wakewoman raises a hand, gently pressing her warm palm to the frightened woman's forehead. It is just a normal, casual gesture, yet the woman gradually calms down.

steps.name: Friendly Resident
steps.text: Okay, okay. I believe you. Right, I still have my hand, as well as my blessing.

steps.name: The Wakewoman
steps.text: It's almost nightfall. You should head back home.

steps.name: The Wakewoman
steps.text: And Reed, you have another banquet to attend, don't you?

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: A banquet?

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: ...Right, the banquet.

steps.name: The Wakewoman
steps.text: So please, allow me to lead the way.

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: Wakewoman, since you've returned, does that mean Moran and the others have already settled in?

steps.name: The Wakewoman
steps.text: That's right. They'll be staying just outside the ruins. They're probably still clearing out the empty houses right about now.

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: Thank you.

steps.name: The Wakewoman
steps.text: Don't mention it. By the way, call me Nemos. I hardly do any work as a wakewoman these days.

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: Alright, Nemos. You mentioned a banquet just now. Who's hosting it?

steps.name: Nemos
steps.text: In a few days, Dublinn will be hosting a celebratory banquet, and all the high-ranking nobles will be in attendance, including Her Highness Eblana. We've been very busy with all the preparations.

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: A celebratory banquet? While the residents are making do with 'stewed meat' and 'grilled fins' made from only potatoes?

steps.name: Nemos
steps.text: The potato thing started out due to a food shortage, but now, they're just...

steps.name: Nemos
steps.text: used to it.

steps.name: Nemos
steps.text: But Dublinn is aware of the situation in the city. They're calling it a 'banquet', but I didn't see any eating or drinking on the itinerary.

steps.name: Nemos
steps.text: I'm not trying to cover for anyone, Miss Loughshinny. I truly believe that Dublinn wouldn't turn its back on the people of Tara like that.

steps.name: Nemos
steps.text: Now if you'll excuse me, I must be going.

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: She certainly left in a hurry.

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: So if directly removing the violet flames would only cause a panic, what if I were to do it more subtly...?

steps.name: Voice from Behind
steps.text: To lunder whatever you want, then?

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: Who's there?
The noble red dragon turns around and sees a figure engulfed in blazing purple flames.

No, if the other residents have been merely 'kissed' by the flames, then the person standing before her seems to have been forged from the purple fire itself. The flames don't look harsh, yet they distort the very light around them.

steps.name: The Exiled King
steps.text: Unfortunately, what you want sounds incredibly boring.

steps.name: The Exiled King
steps.text: After all, Tara's flames have already been dyed that color. That's just a fact.

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: You know about the flames.

steps.name: The Exiled King
steps.text: I happened to find out about them, yes.

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: Tell me everything you know. It's extremely important.

steps.name: The Exiled King
steps.text: Why should I?

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: I need to stop people from being engulfed by the purple flames.

steps.name: The Exiled King
steps.text: So you can replace them with your own flames?

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: As long as the people of the city are safe, the color doesn't matter.

steps.name: The Exiled King
steps.text: What grandiose nonsense. It's almost nostalgic. Your excuse is so clumsy that it's laughable, red dragon.

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: What is your relationship to my sister, sir?
Loughshinny takes a step forward, while the figure moves backwards, preserving the distance between them.

steps.name: The Exiled King
steps.text: Relationship? You, your sister, and I are all cut from the same cloth. We all crave power, conflict, and bloodshed.

steps.name: The Exiled King
steps.text: We're all itching for what comes next, eager to set the land ablaze.

steps.name: The Exiled King
steps.text: But this time, I'll stay out of it. Until the Lair is consumed by flames, I'll be cheering on both sides.

steps.name: The Exiled King
steps.text: Goodbye—

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: Wait!
The red dragon tries to weave the flames of life into a cage, but before it can take shape, the strange figure scatters in the wind.
Her fire only briefly illuminated his long tail...
Then returned to nothingness.

steps.name: Worried Resident
steps.text: Sir.

steps.name: 'The Bureaucrat'
steps.text: It's you. What's wrong? Why have you come to see me now?

steps.name: 'The Bureaucrat'
steps.text: Don't tell me there's another problem with your grain shop that I have to deal with. I've never treated you as a subordinate—we're 'business partners', understand?

steps.name: Worried Resident
steps.text: I understand.

steps.name: 'The Bureaucrat'
steps.text: Good, as long as you do. I have another shipment that needs to be escorted out of the city. Leave soon, and be back before curfew.

steps.name: Worried Resident
steps.text: Sir, about that—

steps.name: 'The Bureaucrat'
steps.text: About what?

steps.name: Worried Resident
steps.text: About the grain we sent out before... You said it wouldn't affect the city's food supply, but now we're all stuck eating only potatoes...

steps.name: 'The Bureaucrat'
steps.text: Do you know what it's like in other parts of Tara? They don't even have potatoes!

spans.text: Do you know what it's like in other parts of Tara? They don't even

steps.name: 'The Bureaucrat'
steps.text: Na Saoirsí's agricultural output is already top-tier. We're taking urgent measures to help our countrymen. Understand?

steps.name: 'The Bureaucrat'
steps.text: Besides, how much did you earn from just those last two carts?

steps.name: 'The Bureaucrat'
steps.text: Look at it this way: the people of Na Saoirsí aren't starving. At least they've got potatoes to fill their bellies.

steps.name: 'The Bureaucrat'
steps.text: What's more, it's almost harvest time. There will be plenty of new grain then. I'm more worried that your tiny shop won't have the throughput to sell it all.

steps.name: 'The Bureaucrat'
steps.text: Still, I'm not one to force anyone to act against their conscience. If you really feel that bad about it, you can always just transfer your business license to someone else and close your shop.

steps.name: Worried Resident
steps.text: But how will I eat then?

steps.name: 'The Bureaucrat'
steps.text: I told you, you're not my subordinate. How is that my problem?

steps.name: 'The Bureaucrat'
steps.text: Alright, alright, just hand over your business license by the end of the day—

steps.name: Worried Resident
steps.text: No! Don't! Okay! I'll do it.

steps.name: 'The Bureaucrat'
steps.text: Hmph.

steps.name: Worried Resident
steps.text: *Sigh*...

steps.name: 'The Bureaucrat'
steps.text: Why are you still standing there?

steps.name: Worried Resident
steps.text: I have something else to discuss. My friend told me that lately, the dark mist in the forest...

steps.name: 'The Bureaucrat'
steps.text: Dark mist? If I needed you to remind me about that, I might as well quit right now.

spans.text: to remind me about that, I might as well quit right now.

steps.name: 'The Bureaucrat'
steps.text: There will be someone waiting for you once you're past the gates, just like always. Anything else is none of your concern. Now go.

steps.name: Frantic Soldier
steps.text: Sir.

steps.name: 'The Bureaucrat'
steps.text: What is it? Did The Brigadier say something when he was on patrol this morning?

steps.name: Frantic Soldier
steps.text: No sir, he didn't come around this morning. The Leader sent him on another assignment.

steps.name: 'The Bureaucrat'
steps.text: Phew.

steps.name: 'The Bureaucrat'
steps.text: Then what's got you in such a panic?

steps.name: Frantic Soldier
steps.text: It's officially harvest season for the agricultural plate to the south.

steps.name: 'The Bureaucrat'
steps.text: Isn't that a good thing?

steps.name: Frantic Soldier
steps.text: Yes, but, uh, all the skilled agricultural workers have left the city.

steps.name: 'The Bureaucrat'
steps.text: Tch, just follow the handbook—do exactly as it says, got it?

steps.name: Frantic Soldier
steps.text: Yes sir!

steps.name: 'The Bureaucrat'
steps.text: By the way, what's the estimated yield for the entire plate? Report it to me, and I'll consolidate the numbers later.

steps.name: Frantic Soldier
steps.text: Um, we're not exactly familiar with this sort of work either...

steps.name: 'The Bureaucrat'
steps.text: You're useless! Can't you at least tell when the crops are ready for harvest?

steps.name: Frantic Soldier
steps.text: They're definitely ripe, or we wouldn't have harvested them in the first place...

steps.name: 'The Bureaucrat'
steps.text: Then isn't it just business as usual? Report a normal yield based on previous years! Now get going!

steps.name: Brigid
steps.text: Hello, I'm Brigid the nomad.

steps.name: Jittery Guard
steps.text: What do you want?

steps.name: Brigid
steps.text: I've delivered all my letters in Na Saoirsí. So I'd like to go to the highest point in the city and let the wind carry my message to my brothers and sisters. Then I'll be on my way.

steps.name: Jittery Guard
steps.text: Ah, now I remember—it's you. You've been here so many times, and we've never let you up there even once. Haven't you learned your lesson yet?

spans.text: . You've been here so many times, and we've never let you up there even once. Haven't you learned your lesson yet?

steps.name: Brigid
steps.text: Even the Victorians let me up to the top of the citadel when they were in charge.

steps.name: Jittery Guard
steps.text: Do I look like a Victorian to you?

steps.name: Brigid
steps.text: No. You're a Taran.

steps.name: Jittery Guard
steps.text: Then you should know that, since we're all Tarans, there's no need to indulge those outdated customs of yours anymore. All that nomad and wakeman nonsense—it's all stupid superstition.

steps.name: Jittery Guard
steps.text: Now get moving! If you don't, I might just have you arrested!

steps.name: Brigid
steps.text: Fine, I'm going. No need to make a fuss...

steps.name: Brigid
steps.text: Welp, I've done exactly nothing I set out to do, other than delivering my letters.

steps.name: Brigid
steps.text: Oh well. At least I'm out of the city before curfew. Now to just pass through the Dark Woods and I'll be back on the open plains.

steps.name: Brigid
steps.text: *Sigh*... I just hope the mist will let me through.

steps.name: Brigid
steps.text: But it's never stopped the nomads before, so why am I worrying about it?
The nomad kicks a pile of fallen leaves by the roadside. The rustling sound echoes through the vast, empty forest ahead.
To her surprise, the sound doesn't fade away—it echoes back in a repeating loop.
Brigid suddenly crouches down, trying to cover the scattered leaves before her. Where the sound is coming from.

steps.name: Brigid
steps.text: Sorry, shouldn't have kicked you.
The sound continues.

steps.name: Brigid
steps.text: Uh—
It doesn't stop. Instead it grows louder and louder, echoing until it becomes an unbearable, deafening cacophony.
At the same time, the dark mist creeps up from her feet, covering her eyes and ears.
Until she realizes she is back at the forest entrance.

steps.name: Brigid
steps.text: ....This is the fifth time!

steps.name: Brigid
steps.text: Not going to let me leave? Really? Forcing me back into the city, is that it?

steps.name: Brigid
steps.text: Hmph. Well, I'm not going back.

steps.name: Brigid
steps.text: I'll set up a tent outside the forest if I have to. I'll get my chance to leave, sooner or later.
